chunks: I [Muyassar] said [to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)]: [What is meant by] the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'And do not cause corruption on the earth after it has been set in order'?

He said: So he [the Imam] said: O Muyassar, verily the earth was in a state of corruption, so God, Mighty and Majestic, corrected it through His Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family),
and [then] He said: 'And do not cause corruption on the earth after it has been set in order.'

key_terms.الإصلاح: Reformation, setting in order — here referring to the divine correction achieved through the Prophet's mission
key_terms.الإفساد في الأرض: Causing corruption on the earth — a Quranic concept encompassing moral, spiritual, and social disorder
key_terms.فاسدة: Corrupt, disordered — describing the pre-Islamic state of the earth

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the meaning of 'Do not cause corruption on the earth after it has been set in order' (Quran 7:56)?
ai.summary: Muyassar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz asked Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) about the meaning of Quran 7:56 — the prohibition against causing corruption on the earth after it has been set in order. The Imam explained that this verse was revealed in the context of the Prophet's mission: the earth had been in a state of moral and spiritual corruption (fasad), and God corrected it by sending the Prophet (SAWW). The divine prohibition that follows is therefore specifically addressed to those who would corrupt the earth after this prophetic reformation — making disobedience to the Prophet's legacy a form of the very corruption the verse condemns.
